- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days) and model forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven overreaction lag.  
- If sentiment turns bearish sharply (e.g., -0.67+ drop in 1–2 days) and model forecast remains flat or rises, reduce forecast by 3–8% to avoid overconfidence in negative sentiment.  
- When sentiment change is volatile (e.g., ±0.67+ swings in 3+ consecutive days), apply mean reversion: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10%; if below, raise by 5–10%.  
- If news volume is low (0.0 or 1.0) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overreacting to low-activity periods.  
- If model forecast spikes >15% above recent 14-day average and sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish, apply “overshoot correction”: reduce by 10–20% to avoid overestimating short-term momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 5–10% below model, apply “lag correction”: add 3–5% to forecast to account for delayed market reaction to sentiment shifts.
